title: Introduction (v1)
description: Ridge 1.x documentation. v1 uses a JSON lockfile and a flatter store. New projects should start on v2.
snippet: You are reading Ridge v1 . It is in maintenance mode. Bug fixes land here; features land in v2. A v1 ridge.lock ( lockfileVersion: 1 ) cannot be installed with the v2 CLI unless you run ridge migrate . Keep the CLI on 1.9.x for this branch. What is different in v1 - The lockfile

title: Install v1
description: Install the Ridge 1.9 CLI. Use this only for repositories that still ship a v1 lockfile.
snippet: Pin the CLI to the 1.x line. Node 18 is supported on v1. Node 16 is not. When you are ready to move, follow the v2 migration guide after running ridge migrate with the v2 CLI.

title: CLI (v1)
description: Command reference for Ridge 1.9. Subcommands match v2, with fewer filters and a JSON lockfile.
snippet: v1 supports install , add , run , exec , and why . It does not support --recursive filters of the form --filter './packages/ ' . --frozen exists. --offline exists. ridge gc exists but is not implied by CI. The current CLI is documented in v2 CLI.

title: Content addressing
description: Packages in Ridge are stored by cryptographic hash. Identical bytes are written once and verified on every install.
snippet: Ridge treats a package as a bag of bytes. The address of those bytes is a SHA-512 hash. The store path is derived from the hash, not from the package name or version. Click the diagram to zoom. Why hash, not name@version Names are not identity. left-pad@1.3.0 on Monday is not a g

title: The lockfile
description: ridge.lock is a contract. It records the exact graph, integrity hashes, and peer resolutions Ridge will reproduce.
snippet: ridge.lock is YAML. Ridge never writes JSON for the lockfile: diffs stay reviewable, and trailing commas are not a style debate. Anatomy lockfileVersion is 2 for Ridge 2.x. v1 lockfiles use 1 and a flatter packages map. ridge install will not auto-migrate a v1 lockfile; run ridge

title: Workspaces
description: How Ridge discovers nested workspaces, isolates node_modules, and shares the content-addressed store across a monorepo.
snippet: A workspace is a directory with a package.json that Ridge manages as part of one install. Workspaces can nest. A nested workspace is not hoisted into its parent. Declaring workspaces Globs are matched from the repository root. Nested matches are valid: packages/experimental/foo i

title: Introduction

snippet: Ridge installs JavaScript packages from a content-addressed store . Every tarball is hashed, written once, and linked into projects. The lockfile is the source of truth: if the graph cannot be reproduced, the install fails. If you maintain a monorepo, care about CI determinism, o

title: Continuous integration
description: Run deterministic Ridge installs in GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, and elsewhere. Cache the store, fail on lockfile drift.
snippet: CI should never mutate ridge.lock . Set CI=true (most providers already do) and Ridge will install from the lockfile or exit non-zero. GitHub Actions --frozen is redundant when CI=true , and explicit when it is not. Caching rules Cache the store , not node modules . node modules

title: Migrate from npm
description: Convert an npm or Yarn project to Ridge without changing application code. Import the existing lockfile, then freeze it.
snippet: Ridge reads package-lock.json and yarn.lock as import sources. It does not keep them around after the first successful ridge install . Import ridge migrate never deletes node modules . Remove it yourself after you are satisfied: What changes Scripts stay the same. Replace npm ci

title: Configuration
description: Every key in ridge.toml — store path, install policy, registry mirrors, and workspace globs.
snippet: Ridge reads ridge.toml from the repository root. Environment variables override file values. There is no user-level config file on purpose: two checkouts of the same repo must install the same graph. Schema Environment overrides | Variable | Overrides | | --- | --- | | RIDGE STOR
